t: Gaiseric took Carthage without a fight in 439, while most of its people were at the races in the hippodrome, and styled himself King of the Vandals and Alans.
The kingdom's fleet looted the coasts of both Roman empires for decades, sacked Rome in 455 and destroyed a combined imperial fleet at Cape Bon in 468 with fire ships.
The Vandal kings were Arian Christians: Huneric exiled almost 5,000 Nicene clergy into the desert and in 483 ordered every Nicene church closed and its property confiscated.
dyk: The best Vandal warriors ended their days as five cavalry regiments, the Vandali Iustiniani, on the Persian frontier of the empire that had destroyed their kingdom.
ev: Gaiseric leads the Vandals and Alans across from Hispania to Africa and besieges Hippo Regius, where Saint Augustine dies on 28 August 430.
A treaty with Valentinian III grants the Vandals coastal Numidia and parts of Mauretania.
Gaiseric breaks the treaty, captures Carthage without a fight and makes it his capital.
A second treaty gives the Vandals Byzacena, Tripolitania and part of Numidia and confirms their hold on Proconsular Africa.
The Vandals sack Rome, carrying off the empress Licinia Eudoxia, her daughters and the spoils of the Temple in Jerusalem.
At Cape Bon the Vandals destroy the Western fleet and part of the Eastern fleet sent to overthrow them.
Gaiseric dies at 88; his son Huneric succeeds and from 482 persecutes Nicene Christians and Manichaeans.
Gelimer, besieged at Mount Pappua after the defeats at Ad Decimum and Tricamarum, surrenders to the Byzantines.

f.predecessor: The Western Roman provinces of Africa (Numidia, Mauretania, Africa Proconsularis, Byzacena, Tripolitania)
f.successor: The Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire, after the Vandalic War of 533–534
